question: What is the primary purpose of a questionnaire in nursing research?

options.C: To replace direct clinical observation entirely
options.D: To gather structured data using written prompts

explanation: Questionnaires are systematic instruments built with written prompts to collect information directly from respondents for research and assessment purposes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why are questionnaires particularly useful in large-scale healthcare studies?

options.A: They allow data collection from many respondents simultaneously
options.B: They guarantee a 100 percent response rate from patients
options.C: They completely eliminate all forms of respondent bias
options.D: They require no prior planning or validation testing

explanation: The standardized nature and written format enable researchers to distribute the tool to widespread populations quickly and efficiently. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h1)

question: What type of questionnaire item provides pre-determined choices for the respondent?
explanation: Closed-ended items restrict answers to a set of fixed choices designed to simplify quantitative data aggregation. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h2)

question: A researcher wants to measure the exact degree of patient satisfaction on a five-point scale ranging from strongly disagree to strongly agree. Which format is most appropriate?
explanation: A Likert scale is specifically structured to measure attitudes and degrees of agreement along a multi-point continuum. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h2)

question: What is a double-barreled question?

options.A: A question that requires both a verbal and written reply
options.B: A question that asks two different things at the same time
options.C: A question with two identical answer choices
options.D: A survey item written in two different languages

explanation: Double-barreled items combine multiple concepts into one sentence, making it impossible for the respondent to answer accurately if their views differ on each part. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why should sensitive questions or demographic details generally not be placed at the very beginning of a questionnaire?

options.A: It is illegal to ask personal questions in healthcare research
options.B: It can trigger anxiety or survey fatigue before rapport is established
options.C: It prevents the use of Likert scales later in the instrument
options.D: It automatically invalidates all subsequent statistical calculations

explanation: Starting with demanding or personal items can alienate respondents, whereas easing them into the survey builds trust and improves completion rates. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h3)

question: What statistical coefficient is most commonly used to test the internal consistency of a questionnaire?
explanation: Cronbach's alpha is the standard metric used to determine how closely related a set of test items are as a group, reflecting internal consistency. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h4)

question: What does a high degree of validity indicate about a research questionnaire?

options.A: The survey can be administered digitally without internet access
options.B: The questions are brief and free of grammatical errors
options.C: The instrument accurately measures the specific concept it was designed to measure
options.D: The questionnaire will produce identical scores regardless of who takes it

explanation: Validity addresses the truthfulness and accuracy of the measurement, ensuring the tool captures the intended theoretical construct. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h4)

question: Which administration mode is most likely to reduce interviewer bias?
explanation: When respondents complete the form independently without a researcher present, the opportunity for the interviewer to influence answers is removed. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of relying exclusively on web-based digital questionnaires in certain developing community settings?

options.A: Excessive printing and paper costs for the research institution
options.B: Immediate mandatory requirement for face-to-face clinical trials
options.C: Complete inability to utilize closed-ended question formats
options.D: Potential exclusion of populations with limited digital access or literacy

explanation: Digital divides mean electronic surveys often miss vulnerable or rural groups who lack smartphones, internet connectivity, or technological literacy. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a pilot study for a questionnaire?

options.A: To secure permanent ethical approval from the government
options.B: To publish the final research findings ahead of schedule
options.C: To identify flaws, ambiguity, and practical issues before the main study
options.D: To substitute for the actual sample size required by statistics

explanation: Piloting tests the feasibility and clarity of the instrument so modifications can be made prior to full data collection. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h6)

question: What should generally be done with the data collected during the questionnaire piloting phase?

options.A: Merge it directly into the final published results
options.B: Use it exclusively to calculate participant monetary stipends
options.C: Exclude it from the final research data analysis
options.D: Publish it separately as a distinct clinical trial

explanation: Because pilot testing often leads to revisions and question adjustments, combining pilot data with final data would compromise research consistency. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical requirement for questionnaire-based research?

options.C: The right to withdraw at any time
options.D: Mandatory participation of all available patients

explanation: Participation in research must always be entirely voluntary, and forcing individuals to take part violates fundamental ethical research codes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h7)

question: What is the key distinction between anonymity and confidentiality in survey research?

options.A: Anonymity means no identifying data is collected, while confidentiality means identifiers are protected
options.B: There is no practical difference between the two terms in clinical studies
options.C: Confidentiality applies only to digital questionnaires, whereas anonymity applies to paper
options.D: Anonymity is legally required, but confidentiality is entirely optional for nurses

explanation: An anonymous survey collects zero identifying marks, whereas a confidential survey collects names or codes but promises to keep them strictly guarded. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h7)

question: What is a well-documented limitation of self-reported questionnaires?

options.A: Excessive cost compared to running multi-center clinical trials
options.B: Inability to ever use closed-ended questions for analysis
options.C: Social desirability bias where respondents answer to please researchers
options.D: Mandatory requirement for continuous surgical supervision

explanation: Participants frequently tend to answer questions in a manner they perceive will be viewed favorably by healthcare staff or society. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h8)

question: Why might a researcher choose a questionnaire over an observational study?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any statistical software analysis
options.B: To manipulate biological variables in a controlled laboratory
options.C: To efficiently gather data on attitudes and opinions from a large group
options.D: To directly witness physical healing processes in real time

explanation: Questionnaires excel at capturing subjective internal states like beliefs and satisfaction across broad populations efficiently. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h8)
